title: DSH Dragonbyte protocol, version 1
description: The frames of all three hops, in one artifact so a host, a bridge and a tenant cannot disagree about them. ⚠ additionalProperties IS ABSENT AND MUST STAY ABSENT, for the reason dsh-wire's envelope gives: the three halves deploy independently -- a laptop can run an old host against a new bridge, and a tenant's bundle is an immutable archive -- so version skew is a certainty. A strict frame turns an additive field on the newer side into a total outage on the older one. ⚠ `v` IS `minimum: 1`, NOT `const: 1`. The explicit version check runs FIRST and answers `unsupported wire version`; a const here would make that check unreachable and report skew as corruption.

v.description: Protocol version. A breaking change is a new v, never a mutated field.

type.description: Which frame this is. The set is closed: an unknown type is refused by the receiver rather than ignored, because a silently dropped frame looks like a slow peer.

token.description: A refresh token, exchanged for a new device token. ⚠ CARRIED ON ITS OWN FRAME, not in an Authorization header: the socket is already open under the expiring device token, and re-opening it would drop every in-flight call.

expiresAt.description: Unix seconds at which the issued device token stops being accepted. Persisted by the host so it can refresh before, not after, the bridge refuses it.

servers.description: The MCP servers Settings saved for this machine. ⚠ THE HOST ASKS FOR THESE INSTEAD OF THE GATEWAY. It holds a device token, not a browser session, so the browser's `/dragonbyte/mcp` route is unreachable to it; the bridge reads the same document the gateway wrote and answers over the socket the host already has open.

requestId.description: The sidecar's correlation token. Its shape is fixed by the shim so a bridge cannot answer an id the shim would never mint.

path.description: The bridge route a shim request names. ⚠ A PATTERN, NOT AN `enum` OF THE TWO KNOWN ROUTES. An enum would make the bridge's own `not found` answer unreachable — every unknown path would fail here as a 400 and the 404 branch would be dead code that no test could exercise. dsh-wire's envelope makes the same choice for `kind`, and its `v` is `minimum` rather than `const` for the same reason.
